The helper function `defaultPageItemLabel` introduces a hardcoded magic string `'UNTITLED'`. Since `DEFAULT_STUDIO_TEXT_OUTPUT.pageItems[0].label` is already a defined constant and guaranteed to exist by the `MeechieStudioTextOutput` contract (which requires at least 2 items), it is better to avoid introducing new magic strings as fallbacks. If a fallback is truly needed for defensive purposes, it should be defined as a named constant at the module scope.

```suggestion
const defaultPageItemLabel = (): string => DEFAULT_STUDIO_TEXT_OUTPUT.pageItems[0].label;
```

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse error bodies before rejecting non-2xx responses**

`postJson` now throws on `!response.ok` before reading JSON, which breaks the app’s contract-based error flow: multiple callers expect to parse `{ ok: false, error }` and surface `error.message`, while APIs intentionally return non-2xx with structured bodies (for example `runGeneratePipeline` returns HTTP 400 with `ok: false` in `src/lib/core/generate-pipeline.ts`). With this change, those domain errors are replaced by generic `HTTP <status>` messages, so validation/provider failures lose actionable user feedback across tool/generate flows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

_🧹 Nitpick_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Consider capturing the error response body and URL for better debugging.**

The current error message includes the HTTP status code and status text, which is helpful. However, API error responses often contain valuable debugging information in the response body (e.g., validation errors, detailed error messages). Additionally, including the URL in the error message would make it easier to identify which endpoint failed when multiple API calls are in flight.




<details>
<summary>🔍 Proposed enhancement to include URL and response body</summary>

```diff
 	if (!response.ok) {
-		throw new Error(`postJson: HTTP ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
+		const errorBody = await response.text().catch(() => '(could not read response body)');
+		throw new Error(
+			`postJson: HTTP ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}\nResponse: ${errorBody}`
+		);
 	}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

In `@src/lib/core/http-client.ts` around lines 18 - 20, The error thrown in
postJson currently only includes response.status and statusText; update postJson
to read the response body (preferably attempt response.json() and fallback to
response.text()) and include that content plus the response.url (or the request
URL param) in the thrown Error message for better debugging; ensure you await
the body read before throwing and handle any parse/read errors gracefully (e.g.,
include raw text or parse error info) so the Error contains status, statusText,
URL, and response body content.
```

</details>

`postJson` now throws on `!response.ok` before reading the response body. Several server endpoints in this repo intentionally return non-2xx statuses *with a JSON contract body* (e.g. `/api/meechie-studio-text` returns 502 with `{ ok:false, error:{message: ... } }`), so this change prevents callers from surfacing the structured error message and downgrades it to a generic HTTP status error. Consider still attempting to parse JSON on non-2xx and only throwing a generic HTTP error when the body isn’t JSON / doesn’t match the expected contract (or include the parsed `error.message` in the thrown error). Also note existing unit tests stub `Response` with only `status`+`json`; using `response.ok/statusText` will cause those stubs to fail unless adjusted or the check is based on `status` instead.
